title: Fake Merc Character Study (part. 21): Our bum Hemingway
summary: Part 21 of NH's mocking lolcow series on fitness YouTuber Jason Blaha, covering his live streams, a failed online romance, finances, a possible eviction and his upcoming senior powerlifting meet. Most of it is insult comedy. NH also comments on bought subscribers, coaching-income claims, copyright strikes and senior powerlifting.
claims: Live streams that beg donations for answering questions are the favorite tool of internet grifters
Buying fake subscribers kills a channel: the algorithm sees subscribers who never click and stops recommending the videos
Blaha's channel has about 110k subscribers but gets around 1,000 views per video, a roughly 1% ratio
Claiming $150k a year from online coaching implies 50+ clients, which NH says is unrealistic even for channels with hundred-thousand-view videos
Fit, good-looking men can simply talk to women without elaborate lies
Client spreadsheets NH saw from Blaha were badly formatted Excel sheets, and no competing powerlifter credits him as coach
NH saved $10k in his first year at a modest entry-level job while paying rent and food
In his early 30s NH has nearly enough savings to buy a $130k condo in cash
Copyright takedowns on YouTube can be fought with counter-claims; only a lawsuit keeps a video down
Senior powerlifting records mean little when teenagers and half-bodyweight YouTube bodybuilders bench three plates
NH alleges Blaha has used PEDs for about 10 years while labeling himself natural on streams
Powerlifting is declining in popularity, especially senior lifting
